newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: 11 die in possible Colombian death-squad attacks.
newsitem.headline: 11 die in possible Colombian death-squad attacks.

text.p: Eleven people were murdered in two separate attacks that bore the hallmarks of right-wing paramilitary killings in northern and northwest Colombia, police said on Sunday.

The bullet-pierced bodies of a woman and four young men were found on the outskirts of the northwest Colombian city of Medellin early on Sunday, police said. All had their hands tied behind their backs.
In San Alberto, in northern Cesar province, heavily armed men dragged six peasants from their homes and shot them in the town square about midday on Saturday, police said.
"We are still looking for leads on these killings but this area has suffered problems with right-wing paramilitaries," a police spokeswoman said.

The murders were the latest in a killing spree attributed to paramilitary death squads. Last Thursday 17 peasants were found shot dead in northern Sucre province and three weeks ago almost 40 people were killed in three days.
